boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Chattanooga record (November 23–25, 1863) in the Chattanooga-Ringgold Campaign [November 1863], covering Orchard Knob, Lookout Mountain and Missionary Ridge as the live page's other names indicate. The November 26 pursuit and Ringgold Gap (GA005) are outside this record and not added. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the Military Division of the Mississippi and the Army of Tennessee without counts; the live field reads zero. Bragg wrote to Davis on November 20 that the enemy was at least double his strength, and in his report says he was greatly outnumbered. Cist gives Sherman some 8,000 men in two divisions across the river by the 24th and Hooker less than 10,000 at Lookout Mountain.
claims.rationale: Relative claims and part-force figures; none is adopted as matched opening strength. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Cist says the Confederates had four lines of breastworks: the first taken on the 23d, a second at the foot of Missionary Ridge, a small line halfway up a steep ascent of some five hundred yards covered with rocks and fallen timber, and the heaviest works on the crest with some fifty guns. Bragg judged the position one a line of skirmishers ought to have held, and says the attackers reached the crest exhausted by the climb.
claims.rationale: The works and slope existed before the assault on the 25th; their occupation and defence on the day are commander decisions not credited here. No map verification.

claims.value: Bragg says it was unexplained why Walthall's brigade on Lookout was not sustained by Stevenson, blames the shameful conduct of troops on the left, and credits Hardee and Cleburne. Cist says the soldiers went up the ridge without orders and even against orders, quotes Grant's remark that it was all right if it turned out all right, and argues Grant's plan had reserved the fighting for Sherman. The frozen commanders are General Bragg and Major General Grant; the live heading gives Lieutenant General Grant and Major General Bragg.
claims.rationale: Judgments are attributed to interested accounts; the frozen commanders do not receive automatic sole credit, and the live ranks are not adopted.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. NPS says one of the Confederacy's two major armies was routed. Cist says the ridge was carried in six places ('sis' in OCR); Bragg says all the left except part of Bate's division was routed in rapid flight, while Hardee's command retired in good order.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 12,485 (US 5,815; CS 6,670); the live field reads 12,482 (US 5,815; CS 6,667). Cist gives Sherman's reported loss as 1,989 (1,492 after removing Osterhaus's 497) and Thomas's as 529 killed, 2,281 wounded and 141 missing, printed as an aggregate of 3,951 though the components sum to 2,951 (a computation here), and says the Army of the Cumberland captured 40 guns and 5,471 prisoners. Bragg says his killed and wounded were very small but his prisoners and stragglers larger.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Cist's printed aggregate does not match its components.

open_questions: Grant's, Thomas's, Sherman's, Hooker's, Hardee's and Breckinridge's reports, the returns and the Lookout Mountain passages of Cist remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Cist is an interested Union staff history. Bragg's and Cleburne's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXI, Part 2, are separate families of interested Confederate commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
